name: er7
summary: Parse, query, edit, write, and redact HL7® v2 messages in the ER7 pipe-hat encoding — three independently-versioned Rust crates, from zero runtime dependencies at the bottom of the stack.
context: er7-rust is a Cargo workspace of three crates for HL7 v2 integration work in Rust. `er7` is the ER7 encoding itself: parse, query, edit, write, and split batch input, with a byte-for-byte round trip and zero dependencies. `er7-redact` removes patient detail from a message without changing its shape, by a policy of HL7 paths and actions. `serde-er7` gives every `er7` type a Serialize/Deserialize implementation. None of the three include a data-type dictionary, message-structure grammars, or validation — that is a deliberate layer above, built by the sibling `hl7-rust` project.

Absent, empty, and explicit null are three different facts a field can carry, and collapsing them is the most common way integration code corrupts a clinical record — read the ER7 format page before writing code against any of these crates.
trademark_notice: HL7®, and FHIR® are the registered trademarks of Health Level Seven International and their use of these trademarks does not constitute an endorsement by HL7.

links.title: Home
links.description: A Rust crate and command-line tool to parse, query, edit, and write HL7 v2 messages in the ER7 pipe-hat encoding. Byte-for-byte round trip, zero dependencies.

links.title: Install
links.description: Install er7, er7-redact, and serde-er7: the command-line tools, the libraries, building from source, the requirements, and how to verify the install.

links.title: ER7 format
links.description: What ER7 is: the pipe-hat text encoding for HL7 v2 messages. Hierarchy, delimiters, the explicit null, escape sequences, batch files, and why it persists.

links.title: Paths
links.description: The HL7 path notation used to name one place in a message: PID-5.1, OBX[2]-5, PID-13[2].1. Grammar, occurrence indices, and the four query methods.

links.title: Escapes
links.description: How an ER7 value carries characters that would otherwise be read as structure — and which sequences this crate deliberately leaves alone.

links.title: Command line
links.description: The er7 command-line tool: outline every value with its HL7 path, query by path, or rewrite a message as canonical ER7.

links.title: API
links.description: The complete public API of the er7 crate: entry points, the six-level value tree, accessors, configuration, escape sequences, and errors.

links.title: er7-redact
links.description: Tutorial, help, and examples for er7-redact: redact HL7 v2 messages in the ER7 encoding with a policy of paths and actions, stable pseudonyms, and a report of every position changed.

links.title: serde-er7
links.description: Tutorial, help, and examples for serde-er7: Serialize and Deserialize implementations for every er7 type, so an HL7 v2 message tree can flow through JSON, YAML, or any Serde format. Includes Strict<T>, an opt-in deny_unknown_fields for catching typos in hand-written fixtures.

links.title: Ecosystem
links.description: The crate family: er7 for the ER7 encoding, er7-redact and serde-er7 as tools on top of it, and hl7-2-from-er7-into-xml and hl7-2-from-er7-into-json for the HL7 v2.5 dictionary layer.

links.title: Comparison
links.description: How er7 compares to interface engines, HAPI and the mature libraries, the other Rust HL7 crates, and hand-rolled pipe splitting — including when to choose one of those instead.

links.title: Benchmarks
links.description: Measured figures for parsing, writing, escaping, and querying HL7 v2 messages in ER7 — with the machine, the toolchain, the confidence intervals, and how not to read them.

links.title: About
links.description: About the er7 crate: who maintains it, how it is licensed, how to contribute, and how it is built and documented.
